notes: Basis: Read-only code-plan inspection of out/dispatch/opening-b.json and the same shared renderer, claims, registry and stage code as Treatment A. No pixel was observed; input SHA256 values were not recomputed (no Bash). All bound guides read in full. RECOMMENDATION: build Treatment A first, not B. B shares A's defects 1 to 4 (identity bridging, the s3 cause, the s6 camera reversal and the binding mis-declarations) and adds a failed close. Non-blocking B weaknesses: (a) 10 of 20 shots (about 29 s, about 49.5 percent of runtime) are overhead plain-wall plans with no Bexar plate. place_check exempts overhead framing, so this passes mechanically (wall views 2 of 10 held shots), but the region stands behind only 8 of 20 shots, which weakens the place axis; (b) the overhead plans (CurbPlan, CreekPlan, StreetPlan, LanePlan, LotPlan) are flat filled rectangles and ellipses with at most an offset shadow, no lighting gradient or material finish on the ground planes. LotPlan is a single grey rounded rect with stall lines. This is a finished_art risk to verify at phone scope; I do not block it here because a schematic register is a legitimate style choice; (c) the first frame (curb-plan) cannot read as an airport (the sign is a 58 by 10 bar, there is no canopy or pictogram from above) and cannot show 'no driver'; the airport is established only at 5.225 s in phone-hail; (d) during n6a (28.5 to 32.53) lane-plan has no recall sentence card, so 'The recall says' is unpictured until 32.705, and slowing from above is only a brake glow; (e) creek-plan cannot show the empty cabin at the s3-event-2 reward (15.31); (f) the s8 fleet becomes six caricons with ground shadows floating over a chain-link close in limits-detail, so the update visibly reaches icons rather than the cars seen in fleet-plan; (g) the door swing from above is a 136 by 12 unit rect at 0.62 scale, about 84 by 7 px. Shared non-blocking notes (a) to (h) and (j) to (m) in Treatment A's report also apply, except that B's s4-shot-2 wheel-water keeps the houses.
strongest_frame: s6-shot-2 wheels-water, 32.705 to 36.86 s (shared with A): the car close at the front wheel rolls on at reduced speed into standing water with a wake while 'may' lights on the verbatim recall sentence. The second strongest is s1-shot-2 cab-wheel (2.6125 to 5.225), the empty driver seat and a wheel turning with no hands.
weakest_frame: s9-shot-2 record-wall, 52.775 to 56.335 s: a repeat of the opening's overhead curb plan in which the record card slides in flat at 0.36 scale (about 274 px wide, row text about 9 px native and about 3 px at phone width) while n9b says 'the federal record lists the flood remedy'.

blocking_defects.criterion: quality_contract continuity (do not imply stock illustration is the actual case) and DAILY_PRODUCTION source-example disclosure
blocking_defects.defect: False implied vehicle identity across distinct sourced examples (shared story_contract and hero request). Transition s3->s4 is kind 'same-subject' ('The same empty white car shape reappears in brown water') although c5 reports another vehicle in a different incident earlier in April; s8->s9 says 'The same white car returns to the airport curb it left'; the hero purpose says 'Carry one white driverless car through the film'; B's carries ('The roof pod seen from above on the crossing', 'The same roof pod seen from above', 'The same bay and roof pod as the opening') bind the April flood cars to the October airport car. The identical RobotaxiHero car (top and side) is drawn in every scene with only 'Illustration. Generic car with no brand mark' on screen. Required fix: make s2->s3 and s3->s4 source-example transitions with truthful rendered production_disclosure text on s3 and s4, and rewrite the carries, bridges and hero purpose so the airport ride is not presented as the flooded vehicle.

blocking_defects.criterion: source fidelity: visual certainty exceeds the reporting
blocking_defects.defect: s3 plans the car stationary on a low-water crossing while rain lifts the creek over the slab around it (creek-plan, 13.03 to 15.32: water spreads over the slab, ripples close in around the wheels), then sweeps it in car-swept. A parked car overtaken by rising water is an unreported cause that conflicts with c11 (the vehicle detected the flooded road, continued on its path at reduced speed); the crossing and depth post are unsourced specifics. Required fix: show the empty car already in the flood water and the sweep, without depicting how it got there.

blocking_defects.criterion: ART_DIRECTION motion: reversing camera tracking; modern floor 'motion' is nondeferrable
blocking_defects.defect: viewCam('lane-plan') sets f_y = (1-e1)*780 + e1*(1260 - 0.5*X - 0) with follow starting at 1150 when s6-event-1 begins (28.5). The camera moves the opposite way about 43 px (f_y 780 to about 823 by about 28.95), then reverses and accelerates to 550 px/s by 29.6; the car's screen speed peaks about 705 px/s (about 23.5 px/frame). The lane dashes and verge visibly drift, stop and whip at the entry of the turn. Required fix: monotone tracking from the car's actual entry (start the camera on the follow target, or ease from it), and re-check the e1/e2 joins.

blocking_defects.criterion: sentence-to-pixel binding; rubric hard fail 'a narrated idea that is not bound to an actual rendered item and visible change'
blocking_defects.defect: Narration-picture bindings do not match the rendered subjects (shared board and registry). n5a lists s5-count and s5-total, but B's record-wall draws only s5-record, the desk and the pen; n9b and n9c omit s9-record although curbPlanS9 and curb-return render it; registry narration_views claim subjects their views do not draw (record-wall: s5-count and s5-total; cab-wheel: s1-phone; record-desk: s5-count and s5-total; map-table: s2-zone). Required fix: correct n5a, n9b and n9c subject_ids and the registry narration_views to the subjects each view actually renders.

blocking_defects.criterion: closing_payoff (the closing image answers the opening question) and legibility at phone size; reject an ending that repeats setup
blocking_defects.defect: B's whole close (50.0 to 58.45) fails to show the answer in a readable picture. s9-shot-1 (curb-plan) and s9-shot-2 (record-wall, which also routes to curbPlanS9) repeat the opening's overhead curb plan for 6.335 s; the record card enters at CARD_AT['curb-plan'] scale 0.36 (row text about 9 px native, about 3 px at phone width). s9-shot-3 curb-return puts the card at scale 0.44 (40..374 by 880..1193 px; remedy text about 11 px native, about 4 px phone, underline about 2.6 px), so 'currently under development' is never legible on screen. In the same shot the card covers the bench and the s9-phone item bound to s9-event-3 (bench phone at about 330..366 by 1040..1114). Required fix: end on a framing where the remedy row reads at least as large as A's 1.08 split, keep the phone and car unoccluded, and do not reuse the opening plan as two of the three closing shots.

The chain follows one generic car from the April creek and street incidents to the October airport curb through 'same-subject' bridges, implying the flooded vehicle is the airport ride and that the two April cars are one car. Make s2->s3 and s3->s4 disclosed source-example cuts and rewrite the bridges.

The creek scene depicts a parked car overtaken by rising water on an invented low-water crossing, which conflicts with c11. Show the car already in the flood water and the sweep, without depicting how it got there.

The answer card is illegible (0.36 and 0.44 scale) throughout the close, two of three closing shots repeat the opening overhead plan, and the final card covers the bound phone. The opening question is answered only by narration and captions, not by the picture.

story_review.one_viewing_summary: Planned chain from above: the roof and dome of a white car come up a pickup lane and brake into a bay, the empty driver seat and self-turning wheel are seen from the rear seat, and a phone request turns to 'Arriving' beside the plane-sign curb. A flat San Antonio map draws in and a limited area closes with a '60 square miles' tag. From above, rain rings spread on a creek and water covers a crossing around the white roof, then from the side the empty car is carried off. Water runs along a street around a roof whose amber corners blink, then a side close shows the empty cabin. A recall card slides onto a desk seen from above, an icon grid fills and a 'Nearly 3,800 vehicles' tag settles. A roof runs up a highway lane and brakes, then a close shows the car rolling into standing water as 'may' lights. The remedy row is stamped, a weather tag slides over two rows of roofs, icons on a chain link take checks under an April 20 page, and the overhead curb returns with a small record card.
story_review.opening_to_ending: Opening question: anyone in San Antonio can now hail a driverless Waymo to the airport, so what does the federal record say about the flood problem its recall covers? Planned ending: the overhead curb plan from the opening returns, the door swings out and a 0.36 to 0.44 scale record card slides in. The narration states the answer (remedy currently under development), but the picture never makes the remedy row readable, so the ending does not visibly answer the question.
story_review.weakest_transition: s8 -> s9 at 50.0 s: from a chain-link close of floating car icons taking checks to a repeat of the opening's overhead curb plan; the cut changes medium, scale and viewpoint with no carried subject in frame (the fleet was already reduced to icons) and returns to the setup picture rather than a changed understanding.

code_observations.source_fidelity: Same shared source handling as A: no brand mark, the verbatim c7 sentence and c8 remedy, on-screen numerals traced to quotes, no speed, depth, crash or rider. The violations are the s3 parked-car cause and the one-car identity bridging.
code_observations.recognition: The top view (TOP_BODY gradient, glass panes, ringed dome, mirrors, wheel stubs, offset shadow) reads as a car from above but cannot show the empty cabin, the airport or brake behaviour clearly; recognition of place and of 'driverless' depends on the cab-wheel and side closes.
code_observations.framing: Overhead shots are not Grounded (the episode excludes overhead from exterior), so their bounds are frame coordinates; the plans fill about 88 to 96 percent of the width. In the close the card overlaps the bench and phone. The caption band and SAFE_RIGHT are clear for principal contacts.
code_observations.region: 10 overhead shots on plain wall (exempt from place_check), 2 wall views among 10 held shots (20 percent). The Bexar plate stands behind 8 of 20 shots. The plans draw their own live oak, mesquite and limestone ground, consistent with Bexar.
code_observations.finish: The side and cab views share A's finished hero. The overhead plans are flat-fill rectangles and ellipses with stripes, dashes and offset shadows only; LotPlan and the StreetPlan roofs are the flattest. Phone-scope finished_art risk.
code_observations.pace: Identical timing to A: shots of at most 4.565 s, reward gaps of at most 3.38 s, first change at 0.2 s.
code_observations.disclosure: The production_disclosure chip renders on every scene.
